evidence_quotes.quote: Data analysis was conducted using both quantitative and qualitative methods, using SPSS and Excel, and descriptive statistics were generated on income inequality, literacy levels and access to basic services.
Only 35% of households have piped water access, compared to the national average of 85%, yielding:

In the study, findings show that only 35% of Harijan households have access to clean water, while 85% live in crowded one-room dwellings with shared sanitation facilities, with rooms measuring 10 x 10 feet. Only 15% have legal property security, and that too is outside the area.

raw_response.publication_year_note: Research Square preprint (v1, DOI: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-6596476/v1) with Posted Date: May 7th, 2025 printed on PDF Page 1; no peer-reviewed journal volume/issue year appears. Note also that the PDF lists only two authors (Borun Chandra and Prof. (Dr) Anuradha Parasar), without P. Jain.
raw_response.rationale: Although the study examines caste-based marginalization, tenure insecurity, and piped water/sanitation deficits in Dhaka's Ganaktuli Sweeper Colony using mixed methods (n=150 household surveys; n=1,494 colony households tabulated), the quantitative component explicitly generates only descriptive statistics (percentages, counts, income midpoint arithmetic, and simple subtraction from national averages such as 85% - 35% = 50% water access deficit). No inferential statistical tests, regressions, standard errors, confidence intervals, test statistics, or p-values are reported anywhere in the manuscript. Flagging quantitative_synthesis_eligible = TRUE is therefore overstated.
